sources.title: Exact repository shopping-cart-merge source and verified canonical mapping

claims.text: The preserved source only asks a coding/business-scenario question about shopping-cart merge; concrete identity, conflict, stock, pricing, ordering, persistence and concurrency rules are not preserved.
The candidate labels SKU aggregation, positive quantities, saturation, deterministic account-first order, input immutability and malformed-line rejection as answer-side executable policy.
The exact Java fixture validates cross-cart and intra-cart duplicates, capping, ordering, input immutability, invalid inputs, empty carts and overflow-safe summation.
An independent source-first review found no hard failures, unsupported claims or uncovered preserved-source variants and revalidated the exact code fixture.

findings: The preserved repository source only establishes a coding/business-scenario prompt about shopping-cart merge; concrete identity, conflict, inventory, pricing, ordering, persistence, idempotency and concurrency rules are absent.

The candidate explicitly labels SKU identity, positive-quantity aggregation, per-SKU saturation, account-first ordering, input immutability and malformed-line rejection as answer-side executable policy rather than recovered source fact.

The exact fenced Java equals the saved fixture and independently re-passes cross-cart and intra-cart duplicate aggregation, cap/order behavior, input immutability, empty/invalid inputs and overflow-safe summation under JDK 21.

The answer separates pure snapshot merge from inventory/price/promotion recomputation and persistence concurrency/idempotency, avoiding fabricated production claims while still covering realistic follow-up boundaries.
